whisper.text: For anybody who's been following along, I've been making modifications and upgrades to the VIVOR fastening machine. Here's the latest project that I just finished the prototype for. This is a threaded height adjustment for the cutting mast. It is using an M8 thread, which gives you 1.5 millimeters per turn. So you get a lot of adjustment. So if you turn it a half a turn, you get 0.75 millimeters of adjustment. And I'm going to make a speed knob for this because right now it's a little bit slow for adjusting quickly up and down the mast height. But for cutting, it's perfect. You know, you could just adjust it. A half a turn gives you 0.75 millimeters. A full turn gives you 1.5 millimeters. And yeah, I think that this will really improve the machine overall. If you're interested in getting one of these for your fastening, just let me know. I'm happy to make them as I feel that the prototype is ready for the market, at least for a couple of beta testers who want to put it through its paces. I'm going to make a speed knob for this, which has a handle which you can turn. Because right now it's just a thumb wheel, which allows you to adjust the mast height. But I'm going to make a speed knob that allows you to quickly adjust the height. For now, I've just been threading it like this to adjust the height pretty quick up and down. But a speed knob, I think, will be a nice addition. So yeah, if you're interested in testing this, I do have them for sale. And I would look forward to any feedback that you might have on this. In case you see something that I don't, it might need some improvement already. The height adjustment for the bottom does get pretty low. I'll include a photo in the post. It's not quite exactly level with the base. It'd be for a little bit bigger of cuts on girdles. I'm trying to figure out if... Maybe I need to get the cut kit mast in order to get this as low as physically possible. But right now, everything is bottoming out on the bottom mast support here. I think one of the things I can do to improve this is make this into a CNC version. So make it out of metal instead of plastic 3D prints. And this would get the... what I'm calling the elevator a little bit thinner here at the bottom base. And allow me to bottom out the mast just a little bit lower than it currently does. But yeah, if anybody's interested in maybe getting a CNC version, I am thinking about having some made. But for now, I have these prototypes available. So send me a message and I'm glad to work with you. All right guys, cheers.
